Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting us, and please pass on my best wishes to Margaret for a smooth recovery. We would be very glad to look after her blister packs. I am the pharmacist who will be responsible for her medication file, and I will be your point of contact from here.

1. Weekly blister packs and cost
We prepare weekly blister packs, seven days at a time, with each dose sorted by the time of day. There is no charge for the packaging itself. Margaret would pay only the normal dispensing fee, and at 81 she is covered by ODB for the large majority of her prescriptions. I will review anything that is not fully covered with you before we start.

2. Delivery or pickup
We deliver free of charge within 8 km of the pharmacy, and Mississauga Valley Blvd is comfortably within that range, so we can deliver right to her building. Our regular delivery runs are Tuesdays and Fridays, between 2 and 6 pm. Since you would like everything in place before she comes home, we can also arrange a one-off Saturday drop-off in the morning, before 1 pm. Pickup at the store is fine too, whichever suits you better.

3. Moving her prescriptions to us
There is no form for Margaret to sign for the transfer; we call her current pharmacy and handle it on our side. We would just need the name and address of the pharmacy on Dundas, plus her OHIP health card number, at the first pickup or delivery.

4. The pharmacist call and medication review
Yes, I would be glad to go through her new medication list with you in detail. We do need Margaret's permission before we can discuss her medications with anyone else, so I will need a signed Family Communication Consent form on file. It is a short form, and it simply records that Margaret authorizes us to speak with you about her medications — that way her privacy is protected and we only share information with the people she has chosen. She can sign it at the store at pickup, or we can have the driver bring it out for her to sign at home.

What I need from you

- Would you please ask the hospital to fax her discharge prescriptions to us early Thursday morning? Once we have all of her prescriptions — the discharge ones and the transferred ones — the first packs take about 48 hours to prepare, so a Thursday morning fax means we can have them ready for Saturday.

- The first packs will not be ready on the day she comes home. Could you please confirm with the discharge team that Margaret will have an interim supply covering Thursday through Saturday, and ask them to go through every dose with her, with you helping, until we hand over the blister packs on Saturday? That way there are no missed doses and no confusion about timing.

- I would also like to complete a MedsCheck with Margaret once she is settled at home. It is free, takes about 20 minutes, and I come to her, confirm each medication against her list and make sure the new routine is manageable. I am available Monday or Tuesday evenings after 6 pm and can come to her building — please let me know which evening works best.

If you would find it easier to talk any of this through than to put it in writing, you can reach me directly on 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm.

Thank you for thinking of us for Margaret's care. We look forward to it.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad, PharmD
Community Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
905-555-0148 ext. 2
